name: Nature Domain
label: Divine Domain
summary: A druidic priest with heavy armor, druid cantrips, and command over beasts and plants.
flavor: Gods of nature are as varied as the natural world itself. Their clerics might be druidic in outlook, or they might be crusaders devoted to a single aspect of nature — the hunt, the storm, the deep forest.
playstyle: A heavily armoured cleric with a druid flavour. Charm Animals and Plants is strong in wilderness campaigns, and Dampen Elements is excellent party protection against elemental damage.

features.name: Acolyte of Nature
features.description: You learn one druid cantrip of your choice, which doesn't count against your cantrips known. You also gain proficiency in one skill from Animal Handling, Nature, and Survival.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
features.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
features.description: As an action, each beast or plant creature within 30 feet that can see you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure it is charmed by you for 1 minute or until it takes damage. While charmed, it is friendly to you and your companions.

features.name: Dampen Elements
features.description: When you or a creature within 30 feet takes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to grant that creature resistance to that instance of damage.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 cold, fire, or lightning damage (your choice). This increases to 2d8 at 14th level.

features.name: Master of Nature
features.description: You gain the ability to command animals and plant creatures. While creatures are charmed by your Charm Animals and Plants, you can use a bonus action on your turn to verbally command what each of them will do on its next turn.
